formula: log(EWMA[d^2 * I(d < -1*sigma), hl=20] / EWMA[u^2 * I(u > 1*sigma), hl=20]) where d,u = intraday returns, sigma = 20-day rolling std

def factor_vol_asym_tail_ratio(df):
    """Measures asymmetry in tail volatility by log ratio of EWMA of squared negative tail returns to positive tail returns. Tail defined as returns beyond 1 rolling standard deviation."""
    df_copy = df.copy()
    intraday_ret = (df_copy["close"] - df_copy["open"]) / df_copy["open"].replace(0, np.nan)
    std_20 = intraday_ret.rolling(20, min_periods=20).std()
    down_tail = np.where(intraday_ret < -1 * std_20, intraday_ret**2, 0)
    up_tail = np.where(intraday_ret > 1 * std_20, intraday_ret**2, 0)
    ewma_down = pd.Series(down_tail, index=df_copy.index).ewm(halflife=20).mean()
    ewma_up = pd.Series(up_tail, index=df_copy.index).ewm(halflife=20).mean()
    factor = np.where((ewma_up > 1e-8) & (ewma_down > 1e-8), 
                      np.log(ewma_down / ewma_up), 
                      0.0)
    df_copy["factor_vol_asym_tail_ratio"] = factor
    return df_copy["factor_vol_asym_tail_ratio"]
description: Captures asymmetry in tail volatility: downside tail events (returns below -1 standard deviation) are compared to upside tail events (returns above +1 standard deviation) using exponentially weighted squared returns. The log ratio is positive when downside tail volatility dominates. Focusing on tails rather than all returns may amplify non-linear, regime-dependent features, potentially improving mutual information (MI) while maintaining the asymmetric volatility mechanism. Repaired to handle zero-denominator/infinite output by disabling signal (setting to 0) when either tail EWMA is negligible.
